THE ONE SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE THIS RUN: THE PENDING BREAKEVEN PRINT POSTED AND IT RESOLVED TO THE GROWTH-RISK SIDE. FRED T5YIFR has now published Oct 23 at 2.20 pct (2.19 Oct 22, 2.34 Oct 21, 2.31 Oct 20, 2.32 Oct 19, 2.33 Oct 16). The single most important pending number on this board for the last two runs was whether the violent 15bp break below the 2.31-2.34 band would snap back. It did NOT. A second consecutive session at 2.19-2.20 confirms the break rather than retracting it: the 5y5y forward inflation expectation is now about 13bp below where it sat a week ago, with Brent 3 pct higher on the same day. That is the market explicitly declining to price an oil shock as an inflation shock. Combined with the 10Y holding below 5.00 pct and HY OAS at the month's wides, the board's regime read is now confirmed rather than provisional: this is a growth and cost-of-capital repricing, not an inflation repricing. Tile moved 2.19 to 2.20, trend down. CREDIT - STILL THE MONTH'S WIDES, OCT 23 NOT YET POSTED. The other five remain unverified and Trump continues to call the incidents fabricated. Hormuz flows have reportedly INCREASED, not fallen. SEVENTH RUN OF THE SAME QUALIFIER: no Saudi barrels are confirmed offline despite the Houthi attacks on kingdom energy infrastructure and the Aramco Dhahran HQ evacuation. So 116 is still a risk premium on shipping and headlines, not a barrel-count problem. PICTURE: a Sunday run adds no prices, but it added the one number that mattered. The breakeven did not snap back, so the three-legged signal from Thursday and Friday - duration bid through an oil shock, credit at the month wides, inflation expectations 13bp lower - is now a confirmed regime read rather than a one-day distortion. Nothing in the hard data has broken: claims at a three-month low, LEI six-month rate positive, financial conditions still clearly looser than average, sentiment flat not falling, no Saudi barrel confirmed offline and five of the seven claimed tanker hits still unverified while Hormuz flows rise. What has broken is the price of risk, and it goes into an FOMC on Wednesday with the dovish tail now the live one. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: the Oct 28 NFCI, first read containing both risk-off sessions; the Oct 27-28 FOMC where the risk has flipped dovish; whether HY OAS keeps widening past 340 when FRED posts Oct 23 on Oct 26; whether the breakeven stays sub-2.30 into Fed week or retraces once the oil premium fades; whether any Saudi barrel is ever confirmed offline and whether the five unverified tanker claims are substantiated; whether gold's break below 4,000 extends; rotating the embedded PAT.
